summary:
Castilla y León operates under Spain's national legal framework on gender recognition and anti-discrimination. Its own regional protection layer has been the subject of legislative activity rather than settled law: in December 2024 the PSOE parliamentary group registered a bill for the real and effective equality of LGBTI+ people in Castilla y León, one of three bills the group tabled that week. The bill's stated purpose includes ending the out-migration of LGBTI people from the region, and the group's leader, Tudanca, called for the fastest possible processing.

On 11 June 2025 the Cortes de Castilla y León voted to take the PSOE-sponsored LGTBI+ bill into consideration. The text runs to 76 articles and answers long-standing demands of the region's LGBTI+ collectives. The motion carried; the Partido Popular abstained and Vox voted against. Taking the bill into consideration opens debate, and LGBTI advocates have said they fear the process could stall in committee, which would leave the initiative without effect.

No regional LGBTI equality statute in force in Castilla y León appears in the material reviewed, and no region-specific rules on identity documents, facility access, health care or hate-crime enforcement were identified for the region. A trans visitor to Castilla y León encounters no documented regional-layer rule that departs from the national framework; the open question is whether the pending bill becomes law.
tangentialFactors:
The parliamentary arithmetic is the main variable in the bill's future. The Partido Popular's abstention on 11 June 2025 allowed the initiative to advance while Vox voted against it, and the committee stage is where LGBTI organisations expect delay. The bill is framed around the departure of LGBTI residents from the region, which the sources present as the pressure the legislation is meant to answer, rather than around a specific prohibition to be repealed.

The initiative is one of several equalities bills registered in the same parliamentary week of December 2024, a sign that regional LGBTI+ legislation in Castilla y León has been pursued as a package rather than as a single text.
localsOnly: For people living in Castilla y León, the pending bill is the vehicle for regional LGBTI+ equality guarantees. Its registered purpose is to end the out-migration of LGBTI people from the region, a demand the region's LGBTI+ collectives have carried for years. The group that registered it pressed for the speediest possible processing.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources date from December 2024 and June 2025. Whether the Castilla y León bill cleared committee, was amended, lapsed with the parliamentary term or entered into force is not established by the material reviewed; the region's present statutory position is unresolved on that point. The content of the other two bills registered in the same week is not described.

No regional hate-crime statistics, health-care rules, facility rules or enforcement records for Castilla y León appear in the inventory, and no incidents of anti-trans violence in the region are reported in it. Comparisons with other parts of Spain rest on the national record.
